title: PDA (L→R) shunt increases pulmonary artery PaO₂

properties.Stem (brief): A 4-week-old premature infant (26 wks) in NICU has a moderate PDA. Pulse ox shows 99% in the right hand and left foot. After catheterization but before closure, blood gases are obtained from several locations. Compared with a normal infant, in which location would PaO₂ be higher?
properties.Takeaway (1 sentence): In PDA (usually L→R postnatally), oxygenated aortic blood enters the pulmonary artery → pulmonary artery PaO₂ is higher than normal.
properties.Explanation / Notes:
Mechanism: Postnatal SVR↑ and PVR↓ → L→R shunt from aorta to pulmonary artery. This raises O₂ content/PaO₂ in the pulmonary artery compared with a normal infant. Aorta/LA are not higher than normal; RA is unaffected. Common trap: thinking LA increases, but the shunt dumps into PA, not LA.

Wrong-choice reflection: I initially chose Left atrium; corrected by tracing the actual shunt direction and where the oxygenated blood enters.
properties.One-liner (Key concept): PDA (L→R) shunt increases pulmonary artery PaO₂
